data.title: China's TCL Smart Home Jumps as Global Refrigerator Giant Expands Thailand Plant
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 15 -- Shares of TCL Smart Home Appliances rose after the Chinese white goods maker said its unit, one of the world's largest private-label refrigerator manufacturers, started trial production following an expansion of its Thailand plant.

TCL Smart Home [SHE: 002668] closed 4.5 percent higher at CNY9.49 (USD1.30), after advancing more than 5 percent intraday. The Shenzhen Component Index fell 0.7 percent.

The second phase of the Thailand production base, with an annual capacity of 1.4 million refrigerators, has been completed and entered trial production, the Guangdong province-based company said yesterday. The first phase, which can make 300,000 freezers a year, went into operation early this year.

The new capacity will support TCL Smart Home’s global expansion and improve its ability to respond to changes in the international trade environment, according to the company.

The commissioning of the second phase will help optimize TCL Smart Home’s product mix, better meet the needs of its global market expansion, improve supply reliability and order responsiveness for overseas clients, and strengthen its ability to respond to changes in the international trade environment and withstand risks, the firm said.

Refrigerators and freezers are TCL Smart Home’s core business. The segment generated CNY8.2 billion (USD1.1 billion) in operating revenue in the first half of this year, accounting for more than four-fifths of the company’s total, according to its latest interim earnings report.

Foreign markets account for most of TCL Smart Home’s business. Overseas operations contributed CNY8.4 billion in operating revenue during the period, making up nearly 85 percent of the total.

TCL Smart Home first announced plans to build a refrigerator production facility in Southeast Asia in January 2025. In June that year, it said its subsidiary Homa Appliances would invest in and build the facility in Chon Buri, Thailand, with the planned investment raised to CNY680 million (USD94.7 million).

Homa is one of the world’s leading original design manufacturers of refrigerators. Before the Thailand plant came on stream, Homa’s annual shipments had already exceeded 14 million units.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Link Science to Build Rubber Reinforcing Filler Plant in Egypt for USD149 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 15 -- Shandong Link Science and Technology will invest CNY1 billion (USD149.1 million) to build a rubber reinforcing filler factory in Egypt to get closer to overseas target markets, reduce logistics and tariff costs, and improve response speed for international customer needs.

Located in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, the plant will have an annual output capacity of 100,000 tons of silicon dioxide and 100,000 tons of carbon black, the Chinese company announced late yesterday. Construction is expected to last 18 months.

Silicon dioxide and carbon black are important reinforcing fillers for tires. Moreover, adding silicon dioxide to tires can reduce their rolling resistance, helping vehicles cut fuel consumption and carbon emissions.

Link Science did not mention the target customers of the factory, but based on its semiannual earnings report, its major Chinese and international tire manufacturing clients are Goodyear, Linglong Tire, and Sailun Group.

Egypt is becoming a popular investment destination for Chinese tire makers. On Sept. 3, Linglong Tire’s parent company signed a memorandum of understanding with the Egyptian Ministry of Trade and Industry‌, planning to invest about USD2 billion to build plants to produce tires and related materials, including carbon black, in the African country.

Sailun announced three plans to build and expand its tire factories in Egypt between August last year and June this year, with a total investment of over USD1.7 billion. In May, Chinese commercial tire supplier Aeolus Tyres unveiled a CNY2.7 billion investment to build a plant in Egypt.

Link Science has a designed annual production capacity of 230,000 tons of silicon dioxide and 225,000 tons of carbon black. In the first half of the year, revenues from its silicon dioxide and carbon black businesses were CNY531 million and CNY713 million (USD79.1 million and USD106.3 million), accounting for 42 percent and 56 percent, respectively, of the total revenue for the period.

Overseas market revenue accounted for only 4.4 percent of Link Science’s first-half revenue.

Shares of Link Science [SHE: 001207] closed 1.5 percent down at CNY17.08 (USD2.55) in Shenzhen today.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s Senssun Sinks by Limit on Plan to Buy AI Computing Firm at Nine Times Its Value
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 15 -- Shares of Senssun Weighing Apparatus Group plunged by the exchange-imposed daily trading limit after the Chinese auto parts supplier said it plans to acquire an artificial intelligence computing power company at a nine-fold premium over its market value.

Senssun [SHE: 002870] closed 10 percent down at CNY47.70 (USD7.11) in Shenzhen today. The stock had suspended trading since Sept. 1, after it rose 6.2 percent on the previous day.

Senssun will buy 100 percent of Wuluo Wisdom for about CNY800 million (USD119.2 million), the company announced yesterday, adding that it plans to pay for the acquisition with cash and the proceeds of a share placement.

Founded in Ningbo in 2021, Wuluo Wisdom entered the AI computing power equipment business in 2024. In the first half of this year, it reported a net profit of CNY28.1 million (USD4.2 million) and revenue of CNY304.7 million. As of June 30, its net assets totaled CNY86.8 million, meaning that the transaction price proposed by Senssun represents a premium of about 822 percent.

Senssun was founded in 1975 as a manufacturer of household weighing devices, such as bathroom and kitchen scales. In 2020, it acquired Ningbo Joyson Quin Automotive System, a subsidiary of Joyson Electronics that manufactures and distributes auto parts, and then shifted its focus to the smart cockpit and components businesses.

Afterward, Joyson Electronics became Senssun’s largest shareholder with a nearly 40 percent stake, after a series of share acquisitions. Joyson Electronics’ Chairman Wang Jianfeng is Senssun’s actual controller.

Senssun’s auto parts business has experienced a slowdown, prompting the company to plan a strategic foray into the AI computing sector.

Senssun aims to establish a dual-driven business model of ‘auto components + AI computing’ and promote the application of Wuluo’s products and technologies in the new energy vehicle, charging infrastructure, and energy storage industries, the firm explained yesterday.

In the first half, Senssun's net profit widened 4.4 percent to CNY739 million from a year earlier, while revenue declined 7.4 percent to CNY28.1 billion (USD4.2 billion), according to the company's latest financial report.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: [ESG+20 Sustainability Leaders] OCBC Links Chinese, ASEAN Markets to Advance Sustainable Development
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 15 -- [Editor’s note] With the implementation of international environmental, social, and governance standards, industrial development has entered a new era.

2024 marked the 20th anniversary of the ESG concept. At this important historical juncture, the United Nations Global Compact, the Center for Asia-Pacific at China International Communications Group, and Yicai jointly launched the ‘ESG+20 Sustainable Development Leadership Interview Series.’

This series explores the insights, achievements, and leadership of Chinese businesses in sustainable development and corporate social responsibility through dialogues with Chinese entrepreneurs and on-site visits.

In this episode of the ‘ESG+20 Sustainable Development Leadership Interview Series,’ we spoke with Eng Siong, chief executive officer of the Chinese branch of Singapore-based Overseas-Chinese Banking Corporation, about how OCBC is working to connect China with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, and green capital with the real economy and advanced sustainable development.

OCBC first established a presence in China in 1925 by opening a branch in Xiamen. During the Great Depression in 1932, OCBC was formed in Singapore by consolidating three banks. Now, the lender has expanded to core markets in Southeast Asia, including Malaysia and Indonesia, which have become key destinations for Chinese companies expanding overseas in recent years.

Ang recently visited customers in Indonesia and Malaysia engaged in the automotive, heavy machinery, telecommunications, and resources sectors. Chinese companies are bringing renewable energy and green technologies to Southeast Asian markets, he noted. For example, one Chinese heavy machinery maker brought electric dredging equipment to the region.

“What we need to do now is work with our teams in Malaysia and Indonesia to jointly build a green ecosystem,” Ang said.

In cross-border green finance, OCBC has actively participated in the Common Ground Taxonomy -- a multilateral framework designed to identify commonalities and differences between different green finance systems -- and helped put related initiatives into practice. One example is its recommendation of a green project in Laos by a Chinese state-owned energy company for Chinese yuan financing.

The electric vehicle sector has many brands and may consolidate in the future, and the power battery sector will remain indispensable for every brand, Ang said about industrial positioning.

OCBC entered the power battery industry at an early stage and has divided the supply chain into segments, including cathodes, anodes, and separators, seeking leading companies and business opportunities in each segment while connecting Chinese companies with Southeast Asian markets, Ang explained.

OCBC has adopted an ‘ABC’ sustainable priority strategy, according to Ang. “A as accelerating the transition to a net-zero future; B as bringing impact to communities; and C as conducting business responsibly.”

The bank has also launched the OCBC 1.5° Celsius loan, linking international green standards, ASEAN network resources, and the needs of Chinese industries. The loan is a financing solution designed to incentivize companies to set and work toward science-based, net-zero decarbonization pathways.

About artificial intelligence, Ang said that AI and ESG can be combined effectively. AI can be closely integrated with the green transition, including by optimizing processes to reduce energy consumption and enabling intelligent power dispatch in electricity transmission, he noted.

OCBC’s recently unveiled corporate strategy, ‘The Next Frontier,’ identifies four strategic shifts: the Asian transformation, technology transformation, net-zero transformation, and business transformation. It places ‘ADD’ -- AI, digital, and data -- at the core of its strategy.

OCBC is actively helping build stakeholder ecosystems, bringing high-quality customers into green cooperation networks and using AI and digital capabilities to drive cross-border green business opportunities, Ang explained.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Popularity of Pet Insurance in China Increases as Penetration Rate Reaches 4%
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 15 -- Pet insurance was once considered a niche product, but has emerged as a new growth driver for Chinese insurance companies, with the market penetration rate reaching 4 percent.

China’s pet insurance premium was CNY3 billion to CNY3.5 billion (USD447.1 million to USD521.6 million) last year, up from CNY50 million (USD7.5 million) in 2020, according to a white paper released by Petdata.Cn.

"The growth momentum of pet insurance has shifted from quantity expansion to structural upgrade," said Xu Xian, deputy dean of the School of Economics at Fudan University.

Against the backdrop of an aging population and changing family structures, pets have gradually become important members of many families, Xu noted, adding that this shift has generated diverse needs and risks related to medical care, boarding, and transportation, creating new opportunities in various insurance segments.

There were 126 million registered dog and cat pets in Chinese urban areas last year, up 1.8 percent from 2024, according to the white paper. The urban pet consumption market expanded 4.1 percent to CNY312.6 billion (USD46.6 billion) in the period.

ZhongAn Online P & C Insurance has regarded pet insurance as a key growth driver. The company’s pet insurance premium surged nearly 23 percent to CNY691 million (USD103 million) in the first half of the year from a year earlier, according to its latest interim report.

"There is still a huge market potential for pet insurance, which is a sector we are particularly optimistic about in the long term," Jiang Xing, general manager of ZhongAn, said during the earnings conference call.

The penetration rate of pet insurance in China has increased to nearly 4 percent from around 1 percent a few years ago, Zhu Yigang, head of the pet insurance business at ZhongAn, told Yicai. "We expect that the scale of pet insurance will reach a new level within about five years.”

With rising demand, insurers are striving to innovate their pet insurance products. For instance, ZhongAn recently launched several industry firsts, including specialized medical insurance for parrots and pet cancer. Meanwhile, Ping An Property & Casualty Insurance was the first to provide coverage for high-speed rail transportation of pets.

Competition in the pet insurance industry is shifting its focus to quality, services, and specific needs from scale expansion of single products, Xu explained. For insurance institutions, it is essential to accurately identify the risks associated with different pets at various life stages, ensuring that the coverage better matches the actual needs of pet owners.

However, several industry insiders have pointed out factors hindering the growth of the pet insurance industry in China, such as insufficient infrastructure for pet identification and the lack of standardized treatment protocols.

There is no unique binding relationship between pets and owners in China, Zhu said, adding that the challenge for insurance companies is the same fundamental issue for the entire industry: how to confirm that the pet that purchased the insurance is the same as the one claiming on it?

Chinese insurers have applied nose print technology to identify dogs and cats, but it is difficult to expand it to other types of pets, Zhu noted.

Another issue is standardizing pet medical treatment. Almost all pet hospitals are privately owned, and their treatment standards vary.

There are many and vast differences between pet hospitals in terms of examination items, service pricing, and treatment plans, and these factors ultimately get passed on to the cost of insurance, said Duan Wenjun, head of pet health business operations at Ant Insurance Agency.

This is a key reason why pet insurance is often criticized for having low single claim limits, increasing renewal premiums, and frequent changes in designated hospitals, he explained.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: Shanghai Unveils New GW-Class Space-Based Computing Network Project
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 15 -- Shanghai has launched the "Pearl Constellation Project," aiming to shift part of computing capacity from ground infrastructure to low Earth orbit and build a gigawatt-class space-based computing constellation and a global computing network.

The Pearl Constellation Project was unveiled by Zhou Qiushi, co-founder and president of Orient Space Computing Technology, which will oversee the project, during the Pujiang Innovation Forum's Space Computing Industry Ecosystem Forum on Sept. 13.

Construction on the project will follow a phased roadmap, with in-orbit technical verification starting next year, Liu Jingjing, chief executive of Orient Space Computing, told Yicai. "The first phase focuses on engineering verification and iteration of core technologies."

Space-based computing refers to deploying computing resources on space platforms such as satellites to process large-scale data and deliver information services.

Orient Space Computing will conduct continuous in-orbit technical verification targeting domestic computing payloads, optical computing payloads, new energy systems, and other areas, Liu said, noting that it will verify key technical capabilities of the space-based computing infrastructure through different types of experimental satellites.

After completing phased technical verification, the Pearl Constellation Project will kick off the first batch of satellite deployment and constellation networking based on China's rocket launch capacity and mass satellite launch conditions, Liu pointed out. By 2030, it will gradually build a globally covered, space-ground coordinated and home-made space intelligent computing infrastructure and service network, Liu added.

The service models envisioned by Orient Space Computing include computing resource leasing, token-based billing for in-orbit model inference, and customized development of space-based intelligent computing centers for industry clients, Zhou said.

During the Space Computing Industry Ecosystem Forum, 27 supply chain partners of the Pearl Constellation Project signed agreements to jointly advance collaborative innovation in key links of constellation building, including computing chips, space energy, inter-satellite communication, satellite platforms, computing payloads, and software services. Partners include the Innovation Academy for Microsatellites of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the Shanghai Institute of Space Power-Sources, the Shanghai Institute of Satellite Engineering, Alibaba Cloud, iFlytek, GCL Photoelectric, Jinko Solar, Trina Solar, Biren Technology, and Iluvatar CoreX.

The Pearl Constellation Project will rely on the Space Computing Laboratory of Shanghai Jiao Tong University and unite member entities of the Yangtze River Delta Space-Based Computing Innovation Consortium and more upcoming ecosystem partners to foster an innovation ecosystem featuring government support, industrial matching, and industry-university-research collaboration, Zhou noted.

In July, Shanghai rolled out the space computing constellation "Star Pivot Project" at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference. Led by Fudan University and StarPivot Space Computing Technology, the project seeks to perform in-orbit AI inference on remote sensing and meteorological sensing data.

The Star Pivot Project will be implemented in three phases: verification, commercial deployment, and long-term deployment, with a target of forming a constellation of 1,000 satellites.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: Chinese TV Maker Konka to Voluntarily Delist After Four Years in the Red
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 15 -- Konka Group will voluntarily delist from the Shenzhen Stock Exchange after 34 years, as the Chinese television manufacturer has racked up losses for four consecutive years.

Konka has entered the delisting process, the Shenzhen-based company announced yesterday after an interim shareholders' meeting. The stock [SHE: 000016] suspended trading on Sept. 4, closing at CNY2.46 (37 US cents), with a market capitalization of below CNY6 billion (USD894.1 million).

Founded in 1980, Konka was China’s first domestic-foreign electronics joint venture. It began manufacturing color TVs in 1984. It was the country’s best-selling color TV brand for five consecutive years from 2003 to 2007.

However, with the arrival and rapid rise of mobile phones, tablets, and other devices, the Chinese TV market has been declining since its peak in 2016. Konka tried to find a second growth segment through investment and mergers but failed, accelerating its financial deterioration instead.

From 2022 to 2025, Konka recorded a cumulative net loss of CNY20.3 billion (USD3 billion), with the losses expanding year after year. In July 2025, state-owned conglomerate China Resources Group acquired a controlling stake in Konka and provided shareholder loans worth about CNY9 billion to support it.

Even after China Resources’ takeover, Konka continued to face financial pressure. In the first half of this year, its net loss narrowed 55 percent to CNY173 million (USD25.8 million) from a year earlier, but revenue dropped 27 percent to CNY3.9 billion. The company remains insolvent, with net assets of negative CNY6.2 billion as of June 30.

Given its financial situation, Konka already faced the risk of forced delisting, so the company decided to delist proactively, giving minority shareholders an opportunity to exit, a person close to Konka told Yicai.

China Resources plans to buy the remaining shares it does not yet own in Konka from minority shareholders at CNY2.48 apiece, the source noted, adding that if most minority shareholders exit, China Resources will raise its stake in Konka to 80 percent to 90 percent, making it a subsidiary.

After delisting, Konka will retain its original brand and continue operating its color TV and semiconductor businesses, which will help it more confidently pursue debt restructuring, business streamlining, and asset revitalization without pressure from compulsory quarterly performance assessments, Dong Min, secretary-general of the China Video Industry Association, told Yicai.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Futura Costaglione

data.title: Chinese Carmaker GAC to Issue Shares to Buy Stake in FAW JV, Halts Trading in Shanghai
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 15 -- GAC Group, a Chinese state-owned carmaker, said it intends to acquire a stake in a joint venture of peer FAW Group through a share issuance to promote the integration and optimization of industrial resources between local and central state-owned enterprises and improve the operating efficiency of listed companies, suspending trading of its Shanghai stock for at most 10 days.

GAG has signed a letter of intent with China FAW, a subsidiary of FAW Group, to acquire part of its stake in the JV, the Guangzhou-based firm announced late yesterday. After the deal is completed, FAW will become GAC's second-largest shareholder with strategic influence, it added, noting that the agreement is expected to constitute a major asset restructuring and a related-party transaction, but will not result in a change of actual control or constitute a restructuring listing.

GAG postponed disclosing the JV's name because it involves an overseas-listed firm, noting that it will be revealed in a subsequent restructuring plan. The transaction remains at the planning stage and is subject to uncertainties, the company stressed.

Shares of GAC Group [SHA: 601238] were suspended from trading when the Shanghai market opened yesterday. Its Hong Kong-listed stock [HKG: 2238] resumed trading today following a one-day halt, rising 5.4 percent to HKD2.45 (31 US cents) as of 11.10 a.m., after earlier surging by as much as 15.7 percent.

Established in 1997, GAC has JVs with Japan's Toyota Motor and Honda Motor, while its brands include GAC Trumpchi and new energy vehicle maker GAC Aion. FAW's JVs include FAW-Volkswagen, FAW Audi, and FAW Toyota, as well as owning truck manufacturer FAW Jiefang Group and luxury car brand Hongqi.

GAC Toyota's management had already changed ahead of the restructuring announcement, with Executive Deputy General Manager Wen Dali transferred back to GAC's headquarters and Deputy GM Wang Jun appointed GM of GAC Components.

Toyota's China sales fell 18 percent to about 809,400 vehicles in the seven months ended July 30 from a year earlier. GAC Toyota sold about 341,100 units in the first half of this year, down 6.3 percent from a year ago, while FAW Toyota's sales plunged 27 percent to around 273,700 units.

GAC's first-half net loss widened 76 percent to CNY4.5 billion (USD670.6 million) year on year, while its revenue rose 9.4 percent to CNY46.1 billion (USD6.4 billion).

FAW's sales fell 15 percent to 1.52 million units in the period. In addition, the penetration rate of its NEV sales was about 14 percent, indicating a relatively slow transition toward electrification.

GAC and FAW could complement each other in several areas, Mei Songlin, an industry analyst, told International Finance News. First is market coverage, with FAW focusing more on northern China and GAC on the south; second is corporate structure, as FAW is a central SOE while GAC is a municipal SOE; and third is technology and product portfolios, where FAW has strengths in commercial vehicles under FAW Jiefang and premium passenger vehicles under Hongqi, while GAC has advantages in NEVs thanks to GAC Aion and magazine battery, Mei pointed out.

The rapid rise of private Chinese carmakers such as BYD and Geely Automobile Holdings is pushing state-owned players to improve efficiency through consolidation, with survival of the fittest at its core, industry insiders stressed. Brands lacking technological capabilities, suffering sustained losses, or facing severe product homogeneity are likely to exit the market through bankruptcy restructuring, equity acquisitions, or brand closures, allowing research and development funding, production capacity, and supply chain resources to shift toward leading companies with sustained innovation capabilities, they added.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China’s Expanding Spot Market Puts Premium on Weather Forecasting
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 14 -- China’s expanding electricity spot market is turning weather forecasting into critical infrastructure for renewable energy trading as more wind, solar, and energy storage capacity joins the grid, industry experts said.

Climate services can directly guide grid operations by reducing price uncertainty, protecting assets, and enabling the precise dispatch of clean electricity, Roberta Boscolo, climate and energy lead at the World Meteorological Organization, said during the 2026 Inclusion Conference on the Bund.

China rolled out electricity spot markets nationwide in 2025, with more provincial markets starting formal operations this year. The expansion is shifting renewable energy producers from “living at the mercy of the weather” to “trading based on the weather,” increasing the value of accurate forecasts for managing risks and returns.

But existing systems have yet to fully reflect the growing value of weather forecasting in power trading.

Boscolo said a system-level mechanism is needed to turn extreme-weather risks into quantifiable dispatch parameters through high-resolution forecasting. It should also assess the value of energy storage in supporting the grid and mitigating risks during extreme weather, enabling flexible assets to be appropriately priced.

Putting a Price on Weather Risk

The growing role of renewables is making meteorological services increasingly important to the power system.

The variability and intermittency of renewable power generation have turned meteorological services from an auxiliary safeguard into an essential requirement for the safe and stable operation of new power systems, Xu Xiaofeng, president of the China Meteorological Service Association, said at the Fifth Meteorological Economy Forum.

“The deep integration of meteorological data and energy and power business is creating a new 'blue ocean' of industry with considerable scale and rapid growth,” said Xu, who used to be the deputy chief of the China Meteorological Administration.

Guosen Securities predicted that China's market for power forecasting services will reach CNY1.7 billion (USD252 million) by 2030, representing a compound annual growth rate of 24 percent from 2026 to 2030.

The challenge is turning increasingly sophisticated forecasts into better trading and dispatch decisions.

Amid the inherent variability of weather and electricity loads, the key competitive edge lies in “making better scheduling decisions based on uncertainty,” said Shen Yanbo, chief scientist at the Solar and Wind Energy Center of the CMA.

By combining physical models with data-driven approaches, artificial intelligence can proactively translate potential weather risks into equipment load controls and automated bidding strategies, finding the optimal balance between safety and profitability in highly uncertain market conditions, Shen said.

From Forecasts to Trading

Energy storage companies are already putting that approach into practice by embedding high-precision weather forecasts into their dispatch and trading systems.

Envision Group's staff said at the conference that the company's Tianji weather model can produce global forecasts up to 45 days ahead at a resolution of five kilometers, with updates every 10 minutes. The model is among the top tier in Google’s WeatherBench 2, a benchmark for evaluating weather forecasting models, and leads in energy-related indicators including wind speed and precipitation.

“Using AI technology is transforming energy storage from passive remediation after fluctuations to proactive scheduling ahead of time,” Huang Zhiyong, senior vice president of Envision Energy, told Yicai. Weather changes affect wind and solar power output, which in turn influences spot electricity prices through shifts in power supply and demand.

Huang added that the AI system is in use at energy storage stations in Shandong, Inner Mongolia, Hebei, and Jiangsu, with more than half of those using it in western Inner Mongolia ranking among the region’s top 10 by revenue.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Grandit Jumps on USD164 Million Plan to Boost Domestic High-Purity Quartz Supply
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 14 -- Shares in Grandit surged by as much as 6.4 percent today after the Chinese semiconductor electronic materials supplier said its joint-venture acquisition vehicle will invest CNY1.1 billion (USD164 million) to construct a high-purity semiconductor quartz materials factory to meet growing domestic demand for this high-end material.

Grandit’s share price [SHA: 688549] closed up 4 percent at CNY22.98 (USD3.43). Earlier in the day it hit CNY23.50.

Jingheng Xidao (Shanghai) Technology, which was set up by Grandit and quartz-materials supplier Ningbo Yunde Materials in 2024, plans to build a high-purity quartz materials production facility in Quzhou, southeastern Zhejiang Province with an annual production capacity of 2,220 tons, Grandit said yesterday.

The facility will produce key basic auxiliary materials for integrated-circuit manufacturing, Grandit said. The supply of these materials has long been concentrated in the hands of a few overseas manufacturers.

The first phase of the project is expected to involve an investment of around CNY333 million (USD50 million), with planned output of 720 tons of high-purity quartz materials a year, said Grandit, which is also based in Quzhou. Construction is expected to begin within six months after the land transfer agreement is signed, and the facility is scheduled to be completed and put into operation within 28 months.

The actual investment amount and construction details for the second phase will be reviewed and determined based on the progress of the first phase, as well as business development and market conditions at that time, it said.

The implementation of the project is expected to help establish large-scale supply capacity for these high-end materials in China, while expanding Grandit's overall competitiveness and influence across the semiconductor materials industry chain, the firm said.

Jingheng Xidao was established by Grandit and Ningbo Yunde two years ago specifically to acquire Heraeus Conamic UK, a supplier of high-purity quartz products to customers in the global semiconductor and optical industries, for a maximum consideration of GBP14.1 million (USD18.8 million).

Grandit announced a capital boost for Jingheng Xidao in a separate statement yesterday to fund the project’s construction and technology acquisition. The funds will primarily be used to introduce Heraeus Conamic UK's production technology for high-purity semiconductor quartz materials and establish large-scale production capabilities.

Grandit and five private-equity investment funds will collectively increase their capital in Jingheng Xidao by CNY180 million (USD26.8 million), Grandit said. Grandit will contribute CNY100 million, while Jingheng Xidao’s other existing shareholders will waive their rights to participate in the capital increase.

Once the transaction is completed, Grandit's shareholding in Jingheng Xidao will be diluted to no less than 36.96 percent from 44.75 percent, but it will still remain the biggest shareholder, it said.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: [In Photos] FIM Motocross World Championship’s Shanghai Race Draws Record Crowd of Over 56,000
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 14 -- The Shanghai round of the FIM Motocross World Championship attracted more than 56,000 spectators over its three-day run, which ended yesterday, setting a new attendance record since the event was first held in the Chinese megacity in 2019.

The competition featured four classes, namely MXGP, MX2, 250CC and 85CC, and brought together 33 teams and more than 90 professional riders from 22 countries and regions. Jeffrey Herlings of the Netherlands, representing the Honda HRC Petronas team, was crowned champion in the MXGP category.

The event also featured strong Chinese elements. The JHL Moto team from Chongqing made its MXGP debut as a manufacturer-backed team, becoming the first Chinese team to participate in a world-class motocross event.

And Zhang Qingtian, the son of Zhang Xue, founder of Chinese motorcycle manufacturer ZX Moto, competed in the 85cc category for young riders. ZX Moto gained prominence this year after becoming the first Chinese team to win a race in the Superbike World Championship.

Riders rev their bikes at the starting line as they wait for the race to begin.

Spectators fill almost every seat in the stands.

Riders kick up large clouds of dust as they race around the track.

Zhang Qingtian competes in the 85cc class.

Riders hurtle past the finish line.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Kim Taylor

data.title: Shandong to Let Power Prices Fall Further Below Zero as China Expands Spot Trading
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 14 -- Shandong, China’s second-largest province by installed photovoltaic capacity, plans to allow wholesale electricity prices to fall further below zero when supply exceeds demand, as China accelerates the development of its power spot market.

The province in eastern China plans to lower the minimum electricity offer price to minus CNY0.12 (2 US cents) per kilowatt-hour from minus CNY0.08 and the minimum market clearing price to minus CNY0.14 from minus CNY0.10, according to a recent notice from the local development and reform commission seeking public feedback. The respective price ceilings will remain unchanged at CNY1.30 and CNY1.50 (20 US cents).

Spot prices are set through bidding and can fall below zero when electricity supply exceeds demand, sending a signal for generators to reduce output. These wholesale prices are not directly passed on to residential consumers.

The proposed change comes as Shandong faces growing periods of electricity oversupply. Wind and solar power accounted for 50.2 percent of the province’s total installed generation capacity as of the end of June, exceeding half for the first time.

Lower negative price limits should strengthen market signals and encourage greater flexibility in electricity supply and demand.

Renewables Drive Oversupply

The supply-demand imbalance is most pronounced around midday when PV output peaks and at night during periods of strong wind generation, increasing the need for flexible market clearing.

The change should support higher-quality market development and shift Shandong’s power market from “whoever generates electricity makes money” to “whoever regulates at the right time makes money,” Lin Boqiang, dean of the China Institute for Studies in Energy Policy at Xiamen University, told Yicai.

Energy storage will see significant development during this process, while coal-fired and PV power will face a substantial impact, Lin added.

Spot Markets Expand Nationwide

The expansion of spot trading marks a further shift from China’s traditional grid-centered power market. Reforms began in 2002 with the separation of power generation from grid operations, though most electricity continued to be traded through grid companies under medium- and long-term contracts.

China began piloting electricity spot market trading in 2017 and entered a new phase in 2025, when spot markets were rolled out nationwide and several provincial markets began formal operations.

The rollout has since accelerated. Anhui’s electricity spot market began formal operations in early September, becoming the ninth in China to do so, following the power grid of the southern part of Hebei in August.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Ugreen Teams Up With Qwen on AI NAS Devices for Homes
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 14 -- Ugreen Group, a Chinese electronics manufacturer best known for its power banks, data cables, and docking stations, has shifted its focus toward smart homes, unveiling new artificial intelligence network attached storage devices developed in collaboration with Alibaba Group Holding’s Qwen.

NAS devices connect to the local area network of homes or companies and mainly store files, but Ugreen has begun adding local inference capabilities through deep cooperation with Qwen, aiming to upgrade them into a personal computing power center that can understand and process data, the Shenzhen-based company announced on Sept. 12. Users can switch to cloud-based AI models for more complex reasoning tasks, it said.

Ugreen’s operating revenue reached around CNY5.8 billion (USD864.8 million) in the six months ended June 30, with that from its intelligent storage products surging 86 percent to CNY770 million from a year earlier, posting the biggest growth among all segments, according to its financial report released last month.

Ugreen will extend its local AI capabilities to the home intelligence ecosystem, said founder and Chief Executive Zhang Qingsen. The ecosystem is an AI of Things hub that provides central storage and computing power and shares computing power and AI capabilities with vacuum cleaners, 3D printers, and other devices through protocols, Zhang noted.

Each household appliance does not need to be individually equipped with AI and computing power because a central hub provides computing power on demand, improving AI reuse and reducing costs, Zhang pointed out.

The global AI NAS market stood at about USD9.9 million last year and is expected to top USD155 million in 2032, for a compound annual growth rate of 49 percent, according to data from QYResearch. Global AI NAS device sales will likely surge to 6.69 million units in 2035 from 60,000 in 2024, with a penetration rate of over 60 percent, China Securities pointed out.

However, whether AI NAS devices can move from enthusiasts to the average household, and whether users are willing to pay for local AI in practical applications depends on future market feedback.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Beijing, Tianjin, Hebei to Co-Build Space Computing Power Industry Ecosystem
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 14 -- Beijing will team up with neighboring Tianjin and Hebei province to jointly develop a space computing power industry ecosystem, establishing an integrated cross-regional computing power network to meet the growing demand for intelligent computing power.

The Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area, Tianjin Economic-Technological Development Area, and Xiong'an New Area and Langfang in Hebei co-launched an initiative to build a space computing power corridor at the China Computing Power Conference in Langfang on Sept. 12, aiming to collaborate on technological breakthroughs, scenario exploration, and cluster cultivation.

BDA will manufacture commercial satellites and carrier rockets, and TEDA will rely on the National Supercomputing Center, which hosts the Tianhe supercomputer series, to integrate supercomputing and space computing power.

Xiong'an New Area, the home of China Satellite Network Group, a state-owned enterprise focused on satellite internet construction, will promote the synergistic development of satellite internet and computing power networks. Langfang will leverage its position as a computing power hub to coordinate terrestrial and space computing power.

With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, China is accelerating the construction of computing power infrastructure. As of June 30, its intelligent computing capacity was 2,185 EFLOPS, up 177 percent from a year earlier, Zhong Zhihong, chief engineer at the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, said at the conference.

China had more than 70 computing power transmission channels at the end of June, with 17 national computing power regional nodes approved for construction, Zhong noted.

Hebei is actively developing an intelligent computing power cluster around the cities of Langfang and Zhangjiakou, which are adjacent to Beijing. The province's intelligent computing capacity has reached 556 EFLOPS, with 2.5 million standard server racks, both figures ranking first among Chinese provincial-level regions, according to a report released at the conference.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Futura Costaglione

data.title: Meituan Launches Its Second Drone Delivery Network in China at Shanghai West Bund
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 14 -- The second low-altitude aerial network of Chinese food delivery giant Meituan has officially commenced operations at Shanghai West Bund, the area along the Huangpu River in the city’s central Xuhui district.

Bypassing congested ground traffic, food delivery by drone is faster and more convenient, a representative for Meituan’s unmanned aerial vehicle business said at the launch ceremony on Sept. 10. It can take as little as 10 minutes from ordering to delivery, cutting waiting time and ensuring food is delivered as fresh as just after being prepared, the representative added.

Meituan entered the low-altitude delivery business in 2017 and completed its first drone delivery to real customers in Shenzhen in early 2021. Its first drone delivery network entered commercial operation in the Chinese southern city in May. In December 2022, the company launched single-route, pilot drone delivery operations in Shanghai’s suburban Jinshan district.

Nearly 20 food and beverage chains, including McDonald’s, Amoy Teas, and MStand, have joined Meituan’s drone delivery platform in Shanghai. The number is expected to exceed 40 by the end of the year.

Drone delivery fees are not fixed, as temporary surcharges may apply due to tight capacity in bad weather, during holidays, and in special scenarios such as scenic spots and parks, a Meituan executive told Yicai. But under normal circumstances, drone delivery fees largely match conventional ground delivery charges, the executive noted.

Meituan’s continuous investment in low-altitude logistics in recent years reflects fiercer competition in last-mile food delivery, logistics expert Zhao Xiaomin told Yicai. Low-altitude logistics can improve delivery reliability and serve as backup capacity, especially in extreme weather, he added.

Meituan’s low-altitude logistics model is not designed to replace ground riders but to supplement delivery capacity, Zhao explained. Successful operations in Shenzhen and Shanghai are expected to help roll out the service in other major provincial capitals and build a standardized, replicable operating model, he noted.

Zhao believes that low-altitude logistics can also test operators’ coordination with merchants. Meituan is likely to expand the service to more coffee shops, hotels, and chain retailers to sharpen its differentiated competitiveness.

The low-altitude economy still faces hurdles, including airspace management, compliance, and safety, Zhang Yi, chief executive officer of iiMedia Research, told Yicai. Other challenges, such as mid-air collision avoidance, emergency landing, noise, and falling objects, still need to be addressed, and relevant regulatory rules remain to be further clarified, he pointed out.

Corporate competitiveness does not merely lie in being the first to fly drones, but also in integrating flight routes, landing infrastructure, aircraft, delivery orders, and safety management into a viable long-term business model, according to Zhang.

Future industry competition will center on technology, scale, customer base, and capital expenditure, Zhao said, adding that operational performance will hinge on sufficient flight routes and scale.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s Yangtze River Delta Sets Up USD186.3 Million Basic Research Fund
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 14 -- The Yangtze River Delta region, which comprises the eastern Chinese city of Shanghai and parts of Zhejiang, Jiangsu and Anhui provinces, has unveiled a CNY1.25 billion (USD186.3 million) fund to address financing challenges in cross-provincial research collaboration.

The fund was jointly launched by the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the three provinces, and Shanghai at the Pujiang Innovation Forum held in the city on Sept. 12. Following the principles of unified funding and joint management, each party will contribute CNY50 million (USD7.5 million) a year, forming an annual pool of CNY250 million (USD37.2 million) from next year through 2031.

China's local finances have long been restricted by policies and can only support local science and technology innovation projects, creating institutional obstacles to raising and using funds once cross-provincial research cooperation is involved. To address the issue, the Yangtze River Delta region introduced the first regional regulation supporting cross-provincial sci-tech innovation collaboration in September last year, proposing the establishment of the basic research fund.

A major breakthrough in forming the fund is the focus on unified decision-making and top-level planning in its mechanism design, Xu Xiaochuan, director of the basic research office at the Shanghai Science and Technology Commission, told Yicai. A special management committee composed of the three provinces, the city, and the NSFC has been formed to review the fund's overall layout plan over the five years and decide which projects to support each year, Xu noted.

The first five-year phase of the fund will focus on biomedicine and future materials, with per-project funding set between CNY3 million and CNY10 million (USD 447,200 and USD1.5 million), Xu said. In addition, compared to traditional natural science foundations that focus on researchers' personal interests, the fund will be industry-oriented, inviting firms to propose topics around global scientific frontiers and major industrial needs, Xu pointed out.

The fund's ultimate goal is to integrate advantageous regional resources to jointly overcome major industry bottlenecks, achieve significant sci-tech breakthroughs with global impact, and promote high-quality industrial development, Xu stressed.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Martin Kadiev

data.title: Tesla Offers Up to USD1,940 Incentive to Chinese Buyers Amid September Discount Rush
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 7 -- US electric vehicle giant Tesla has joined a new round of price cuts in China's auto market, offering buyers temporary subsidies of up to CNY13,000 (USD1,940) that bring purchase costs to record lows.

Buyers who order and take delivery of Model 3 and Model Y vehicles by Sept. 30 can receive cash rewards of CNY5,000 and CNY10,000 (USD745 and USD1,490), respectively, while buyers of designated Model 3 versions can get an additional CNY8,000 insurance subsidy, Tesla China announced today.

After the incentives, the lowest prices of the Model 3 and Model Y in China have fallen to CNY222,500 and CNY253,500 (USD33,150 and USD37,770), respectively, their lowest since the refreshed versions of the two models were launched, Tesla noted.

The move comes as more than 10 automakers have rolled out promotions in China since the start of September, including options packages, cash subsidies, and preferential financing, amid sluggish demand in the world's largest auto market.

Electric vehicle maker Leapmotor Technology, for example, launched purchase benefits worth up to CNY19,680 on Sept. 1, including complimentary interior and exterior options and charging stations. Geely Auto-backed Zeekr recently offered a CNY10,000 insurance subsidy as well as financing and options discounts for its flagship Zeekr 8X sports utility vehicle.

Luxury gasoline-powered car brands have introduced even steeper discounts. SAIC Audi recently announced limited-time September prices of CNY262,800 for its A7L luxury four-door coupe and CNY467,600 for its Q6 SUV -- discounts of 37 percent and 29 percent respectively off their official guide prices.

The latest round of price cuts comes against a backdrop of weakness in China's auto market this year. Retail sales of passenger cars fell 20 percent from a year earlier to 11.8 million units in the first eight months, while retail sales of new energy vehicles dropped 11 percent to 6.7 million units, according to the latest data from the China Passenger Car Association.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Emmi Laine

data.title: Disney to Help Chinese Licensees Open Stores on Cross-Border E-Commerce Platforms
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 11 -- The Walt Disney Company, one of the world’s largest entertainment businesses, plans to deepen cooperation with overseas e-commerce retailers and platforms, as it seeks to help more Chinese licensees set up Disney-authorized cross-border stores that sell directly to consumers in global markets.

Licensed product sales have long been a major revenue stream for California-based Disney, Kermid Rahman, senior vice president and general manager of Disney Consumer Products Asia Pacific, said in an interview with Yicai yesterday during the company’s 2027 APAC consumer products launch event held in Shanghai.

After identifying the significant growth potential of international retail markets, Disney initiated this program three years ago, Rahman said. To date, more than 100 partners across the APAC region have joined the initiative, selling their Disney-licensed products in European and North American markets, as well as in Asia, he said.

Some Chinese licensees Yicai contacted said that under this partnership model, Disney leverages its intellectual property assets in film and television, overseas communication channels, and global partner network to help boost their sales. For instance, around the time of major Disney film releases, it coordinates the launch and marketing of related licensed merchandise, helping partners’ stores land more orders from abroad.

Disney plans to scale up the initiative next year, rolling out joint marketing campaigns centered on core IP assets, key product categories, and critical timing windows, Rahman revealed. “By partnering with overseas e-commerce retailers and platforms, we aim to enable more overseas consumers to directly purchase Disney-licensed goods made by our Chinese partners via these platforms,” he said.

Disney’s Chinese licensees mainly fall into two groups. The first consists of manufacturers such as Bruco, a Shanghai-based toymaker. Many of the firms in this group do not have overseas sales channels and marketing capabilities, so they are the primary target for Disney’s initiative.

The second group involves IP licensing and encompasses businesses that have their own overseas sales networks, such as Miniso, which manufactures products based on classic Disney characters like Mickey Mouse.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Tom Litting

data.title: China Orders Country’s Largest NEV Recall Over Door Handle Safety
data.description:
(Yicai) Aug. 24 -- China has ordered the country’s biggest recall of new energy vehicles, with nine automakers -- including Tesla -- set to bring in more than 4.2 million cars because of safety concerns over concealed door handles.

The callback, ordered by the State Administration for Market Regulation on Aug. 21, is also China’s biggest cross‑brand recall stemming from a single design issue.

The carmakers involved issued recall notices the same day, citing concerns that emergency mechanical door releases in the cars blend into the interior trim, making them hard to identify and operate. In extreme situations, such as severe crashes that cause the car’s 12‑volt power supply to fail, the issue could prevent occupants from quickly opening the doors and escaping, while also making it harder for emergency crews to access the vehicle from outside.

Tesla accounts for the largest share of the recall at nearly 2.98 million cars. The vehicles were manufactured between March 2019 and late April 2026, and include both China-made and imported models. The affected lineup includes the Model 3, Model Y, Model X and Model S.

Others with sizeable callbacks include Xiaomi with 390,500, Leapmotor with 371,200, Xpeng with 264,800, and Geely Holding with 92,658.

The companies are taking different approaches to address the issue, all provided free of charge. They include placing warning labels next to the emergency mechanical releases, using over‑the‑air software updates to enable the windows to automatically lower following an accident, thereby providing an additional escape route, and replacing the handle covers to make them more visible.

China’s national standards for automotive door handles will take effect next Jan. 1. Safety hazards associated with hidden door handles have become increasingly clear, an expert told Yicai. Even though the new mandatory standards will not apply retroactively to cars already on the road, it is reasonable for automakers to recall existing vehicles to address risks, the person added.

Concealed pop-out door handles were first widely introduced to passenger cars by Austin-based Tesla with the Model S. Their streamlined appearance, improved aerodynamic performance, and high-tech appeal led many Chinese NEV manufacturers to adopt the design. But as the design spread, questions around its behavior in emergencies have become harder to ignore.

If a serious accident were to disable a vehicle’s electronic door release mechanism, hidden door handles on the outside may fail to deploy automatically, making it more difficult for rescuers to get into the car. Although emergency mechanical releases are fitted inside, their low visibility and poorly differentiated covers can make them difficult to locate quickly, impeding the chances of occupants escaping after an accident.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Kim Taylor

data.title: China Targets 70% NEV Sales in Passenger Vehicle Market by 2030
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 11 -- China has set a goal for new energy vehicles to account for 70 percent of passenger vehicle sales by 2030, while new energy commercial vehicles are expected to make up 40 percent of commercial vehicle sales, according to a five-year development plan for intelligent connected new energy vehicles released by the Chinese government yesterday.

This industrial development plan, issued by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and eight other central government departments yesterday, also aims for the overall auto industry to reach peak carbon emissions by 2030 and to accelerate the green and low-carbon transformation of the automotive supply chain.

It also called for stronger monitoring and regulation of production capacity in the automobile and power battery industries. It aims to phase out outdated and inefficient capacity in an orderly manner through market-based and legal mechanisms, thereby improving overall capacity utilization across the industry.

China’s auto sector is currently operating below what is generally considered the healthy capacity utilization threshold. Data previously released by the National Bureau of Statistics showed that capacity utilization in the car manufacturing industry fell to about 70.3 percent in the first quarter, before edging up to 70.8 percent in the second quarter. Both were lower than the generally accepted healthy manufacturing benchmark of 75 percent.

The five-year plan calls for capacity monitoring and regulation in the automotive industry and extends such measures to key components, including power batteries, Cui Dongshu, head of the China Passenger Car Association, told Yicai. On the one hand, this could raise the entry threshold for newly established independent automakers and curb the launch of unnecessary new projects at an early stage. On the other hand, it also signals the government’s support for mergers, restructuring and cross-regional consolidation within the industry.

The government’s approach is not to restrict reasonable capacity expansion, but to provide early warnings and guide production capacity to better match market demand, thereby preventing destructive price wars among industry players, Cui said.

The document also calls for autonomous driving functions to be deployed and adopted on a large scale by 2030. It aims for vehicles equipped with autonomous driving systems to achieve significantly higher safety performance than human drivers, and for highly automatic driving to be realized on highways, urban expressways and certain city roads.

The plan reiterated that China will support foreign companies in expanding their operations in the country and fully implement national treatment for foreign-invested firms. Domestic and foreign companies will be treated equally in government procurement and other activities.

The government also encourages Chinese and overseas firms to deepen cooperation in the research, development and investment of vehicles and key components to speed up product upgrades and jointly explore global markets, according to the plan.

New energy passenger vehicles accounted for 54 percent of passenger vehicle sales in China in 2025, according to data from the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers, while new energy commercial vehicles made up 26.9 percent.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Kim Taylor
